newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Alston unworried on Telstra sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Alston unworried on Telstra sale.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Friday he was not worried by a crucial independent Senator's comment that he was now more likely to vote against the sale of a third of state-owned telecommunications giant Telstra Corp Ltd.

Earlier on Friday independent Tasmanian Senator Brian Harradine said he was less likely to vote for the Telstra privatisation bill because of Alston's revelation that Telstra was likely to shed eight percent of its workforce in Tasmania.
"No, this is an issue unrelated to privatisation," Alston told reporters when asked if he was now worried about the Telstra bill.
"This is occuring right now under a wholly owned government body. This is not affected by privatisation," he said.
Alston told parliament on Thursday he had underestimated the number of jobs that Telstra would shed in the state of Tasmania after further deregulation of the industry planned to begin in July.
He said the job reductions in Tasmania would be in the order of eight percent, not the two percent he had predicted earlier this year.
Alston also released a letter he had written to Telstra about the incorrect estimate Telstra had given him earlier. He has demanded Telstra ensure it does not make such mistakes in the future.
The government needs the vote of two Independents, including Harradine, for parliamentary authorisation of its plan to sell one-third of Telstra.
The partial sale of Telstra is expected to raise about A$8.0 billion.
Telstra plans to cut staff numbers by 22,000 over the next three years to improve efficiency in the face of new competition as the Australian market is fully deregulated from July 1 next year.
